summary: Server crash while loading Superflat world based on Rails // java.lang.StackOverflowError: Exception while updating neighbours
description: Steps to reproduce - Create new world - More world options - Worldtype: Superflat - Customize - Presets - Enter preset - minecraft:rail - Server will crash while loading the world Same crash occurs when using the minecraft:repeater preset, just after first player interaction with one of the repeaters. Stacktrace Encountered an unexpected exception z: Exception while updating neighbours at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.b(SourceFile:886) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.a(SourceFile:822) at faq.a(SourceFile:96) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.x(SourceFile:688) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.a(SourceFile:270) at java.base/java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:831) Caused by: java.lang.StackOverflowError at java.base/java.lang.ClassLoader.defineClass1(Native Method) at java.base/java.lang.ClassLoader.defineClass(ClassLoader.java:1010) at java.base/java.security.SecureClassLoader.defineClass(SecureClassLoader.java:150) at java.base/jdk.internal.loader.BuiltinClassLoader.defineClass(BuiltinClassLoader.java:855) at java.base/jdk.internal.loader.BuiltinClassLoader.findClassOnClassPathOrNull(BuiltinClassLoader.java:753) at java.base/jdk.internal.loader.BuiltinClassLoader.loadClassOrNull(BuiltinClassLoader.java:676) at java.base/jdk.internal.loader.BuiltinClassLoader.loadClass(BuiltinClassLoader.java:634) at java.base/jdk.internal.loader.ClassLoaders$AppClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoaders.java:182) at java.base/java.lang.ClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoader.java:519) at bwq.a(SourceFile:361) [...] Server crash log has been included as attachment.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a new world.
3. Select "More World Options."
4. Set "Worldtype" to "Superflat."
5. Select "Customize."
6. Choose "Presets."
7. Enter the preset `minecraft:rail`.
8. Start the world and observe the server crash while loading.
9. Repeat steps 1-8 using the preset `minecraft:repeater` and interact with a repeater to observe the crash.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 1.17.1 Release Candidate 1, 1.17.1, 1.18, 1.18.1
Observed Behavior:
When attempting to load a Superflat world configured with the preset `minecraft:rail`, the server encounters a critical failure resulting in a crash. This occurs specifically during the world generation phase, where the server attempts to update neighboring blocks related to the rail entities. The crash is triggered by a `java.lang.StackOverflowError`, indicating that the server has entered an infinite loop or excessive recursive calls while processing block updates.

Additionally, a similar crash occurs when using the `minecraft:repeater` preset. In this case, the server crashes immediately after the first player interaction with a redstone repeater. This further suggests that the issue is related to the handling of redstone-related blocks in the Superflat world type, particularly when their states are being updated upon player interaction.

The stack trace provided indicates that the crash originates from the `MinecraftServer` class, specifically during the execution of the `b()` and `a()` methods, which are responsible for processing updates to the game state. The `StackOverflowError` is a direct result of the server's failure to manage the updates efficiently, leading to a cascading failure in the class loader when attempting to define and load classes repeatedly.

This behavior is reproducible every time the aforementioned presets are utilized, making it a consistent issue that requires further investigation to understand the underlying cause of the recursive block update calls.
Expected Behavior: When creating a new Superflat world using the minecraft:rail preset, the server should load the world without crashing, allowing players to interact with the environment and utilize the rails as intended. Similarly, when using the minecraft:repeater preset, the server should function normally, permitting players to interact with repeaters without resulting in a crash. The expected behavior is for the game to handle these blocks correctly and maintain stability throughout gameplay.
